Class Animation

java.lang.Object
com.animationlib.api.Animation
public final class Animation extends Object
A named, reusable handle to an animation resource: configured once, then played as often as you like.

Drop the animation file in resources/assets/<modid>/animationlib/animations/ (see AnimationRegistry for the supported formats and how ids are derived from them), then declare a handle for it and set up whatever options it needs: 

public final class Example {
    public static final Animation ANIMATION = Animation.init("modid:animation")
            .cameraFollowsPlayer("right_arm")
            .forceThirdPerson(true);
}

...

Example.ANIMATION.play(player);

Every option setter returns this, so they can either chain as above or stand on their own (Example.ANIMATION.forceThirdPerson(true);) — including later, to reconfigure a handle between plays.

Plays on any entity, as long as its bones (e.g. left_arm) match names actually present on that entity's model. Works on either the logical client (only meaningful for the client's own player) or the logical server (any entity).

    • cameraFollowsPlayer

      public Animation cameraFollowsPlayer(String bone)
      While this animation plays, locks the camera onto bone of the entity it's being played on, instead of onto this animation's own camera bone, if any. Since the camera only ever follows the viewing client's own player, that entity is the player whenever this does anything at all — which is what lets it be configured up front, with no entity in hand.

      This animation's own camera bone position still applies on top, and mouse look is frozen for the duration, like a cutscene. Pass null to clear the target and go back to the default behavior (this animation's own camera bone, if any).

    • cameraFollowsEntity

      public Animation cameraFollowsEntity(net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity entity, String bone)
      Like cameraFollowsPlayer(String), but aims the camera at bone of some other entity entirely, which doesn't need to be the one this animation is played on.

      entity only has visible rotation data for bone at a given moment if it's itself currently playing some animation that animates that bone; if not, this falls back to this animation's own camera bone rotation, if it has one.

      Pass null for both arguments to clear the target.

    • forceThirdPerson

      public Animation forceThirdPerson(boolean force)
      When true, playing this animation forces the client into third-person view for its duration, restoring whatever camera type was active before once it stops. Defaults to false.

    • hideInventory

      public Animation hideInventory(boolean hide)
      When true, playing this animation hides the player's inventory for its duration: the inventory screen can't be opened (and is closed if already open), and the hotbar is not drawn, nor are the health, hunger, armor and XP bars around it. Defaults to false.

    • item

      public Animation item(net.minecraft.resources.Identifier item)
      While this animation plays, the animated entity's main hand shows this item instead of whatever it's really holding (or nothing). Animate it with the item, item_left and item_right bones. Takes the item's id, e.g. "minecraft:diamond_sword"; pass null to go back to the animation's own item field, if any. Purely visual: the entity's real inventory is untouched.

    • itemNum

      public Animation itemNum(int slot)
      Like item, but picks the item from the played-on player's inventory: slot 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the rest of the inventory. The slot is read when the animation starts (later changes to it aren't followed), and only works on players. An explicit item wins over this; an empty slot leaves the real held item shown. Pass a negative number to clear it and go back to the animation's own item_num field.
      Throws:
      InvalidAnimationException - if slot is above 35
